situational_context: Running comeback well established and now governed by an active C4 training block (protocols/active_block.md, rev 2026-07-29, sessions #21-40) targeting a 12 km Beaumonts objective (~30/10). 27 runs logged since May 3, 2026 (104 days in); longest to date is 10.5 km (Run #20, Jul 25, Saint-Malo hills, avg HR 145) — well past the 8-10 km reference set at the previous refresh. The most recent two prescribed sessions came in short of the active block's table (Run #26 Aug 9: 5.89 km vs a 9.0 km SL target; Run #27 Aug 12: 4.23 km easy vs a 6.0 km target), and this past week has been light overall (Saint-Malo travel, one casual sea swim Aug 14) — Garmin now flags training_status as 'Detraining', chronic_load_28d down to ~24.7 from a late-July peak of ~30.6, acute_load_7d at 14.6, ACWR ~0.59 (well below the 0.8 floor). Body weight continues to trend down: 100.68 kg (Aug 11, latest reading), down from 102.6 kg mid-June. VO2max running improved to 42.9 (from 40.6 in June); VO2max cycling shows an unexplained jump to an identical 42.9 starting Aug 11 (from a stable 38.6) that looks like a Garmin sync artifact rather than a real gain, flagged for cross-check next refresh. HRV weekly avg flat at 35 (unchanged vs June, still below the 39-40 mid-May peak). Resting HR has drifted up: 7d avg ~52 bpm (vs 50 in June), with the last 3 days (Aug 12-14) elevated to 52-55 bpm, coinciding with travel — worth watching before resuming full block volume. Sleep improved to 7.98h 30-day avg (from 7.26h in June) - not the bottleneck. No new labs since Dec 2025; the Vitamin D retest that was due ~July 2026 has not landed as of this refresh (mid-August) and is now overdue. MEDICATION (standing, from protocols/health-profile.md): Benjamin is on a GLP-1 receptor agonist (weekly injection, weight-management indication) — initiation decided at the 2026-08-04 teleconsultation with Dr Monnier, first injection estimated mid-August 2026 (molecule, dose and injection day still to confirm). The Aug 12-14 RHR rise to 52-55 bpm and the flat-to-falling HRV coincide with this window and are inside the expected GLP-1 class effect (+1-5 bpm RHR, lower HRV); they must be read against a post-initiation baseline, not the June pre-medication one, and RHR/HRV alone must not gate the running comeback. Appetite suppression is expected: low or absent nutrition logs are a possible under-fueling signal, not only a logging lapse, and the protein floor (T.glp1) applies daily. Weight is expected to fall; flag only loss faster than the T.glp1 band or a high lean-mass share.

medications.name: GLP-1 receptor agonist (molecule/dose to confirm)
medications.interpretation_notes: RHR +1-5 bpm and lower HRV expected (class effect) - use post-initiation baseline and require a second signal before flagging; appetite suppressed - protein >= T.glp1.protein_floor_g_per_kg daily, zero-intake days may be real under-eating; weight loss expected - flag only rate > T.glp1.weight_loss_rate_flag_pct_per_week or lean-mass share > T.glp1.lean_mass_share_of_loss_flag_pct; delayed gastric emptying - last solid meal >= T.glp1.pre_run_meal_gap_hours_min h pre-run; hydration and heat caution; keep >= 1 strength session/week

recommendations.text: Resting HR has drifted from a 50 bpm baseline (June) to 52-55 bpm over the last 3 days (Aug 12-14). This coincides with the GLP-1 agonist initiation window (protocols/health-profile.md): a +1-5 bpm RHR rise with lower HRV is the expected class effect, so it is NOT by itself evidence of overload or sub-clinical illness. Do not gate the active block on the pre-medication RHR; re-baseline after ~3 weeks on a stable dose (T.glp1) and hold volume only if a second signal (sleep, skin temp, symptoms, HR-at-pace drift) agrees. Separately, the last two prescribed sessions came in short of target - check appetite/energy (GLP-1 appetite suppression) before attributing that to fatigue.
recommendations.measurable: Post-initiation RHR/HRV baseline established after 21 days on a stable dose; next 2 sessions completed at target with no second recovery signal off; protein >= 1.6 g/kg logged on >= 5 of 7 days

markers_to_watch.threshold: Flag if 14-day loss rate > T.glp1.weight_loss_rate_flag_pct_per_week (1.5 %/wk) or Withings muscle-mass share of the loss > T.glp1.lean_mass_share_of_loss_flag_pct (35 %); a downward trend inside the 0.5-1.0 %/wk band is expected and is not a signal
markers_to_watch.reason: Weight loss is the therapeutic goal of the GLP-1 agonist; the athletic risk is the lean-mass share and too-rapid loss (gallstones, RED-S), not the loss itself
